what_this_is: The minimum causal facts from three private records on one declared synthetic repairable case, each proof run once, under a diagnostic read bound of one read per call. A memoryless control chose the same unproductive diagnostic on every call and stayed unresolved 3 of 3. With Decision Receipts, Run 1 made that same choice, spent its one read, stayed unresolved, and the verifier stored a Decision Receipt for the dead end. Run 2 is a new call on the same problem: the controller matched that receipt and precluded only the proven dead end before the first Decider request, Decider 2B then made one fresh choice over the three remaining diagnostics, the call spent one read, applied the repair and verified it. No second Decider call was made.
what_this_is_not: Not a rate, a benchmark, a statistical result, an accuracy figure or a cost claim: n = 1 case, and one sequence per proof. Not model learning: the checkpoint is unchanged between calls, and it chose the dead end on its first exposure to the full option set. Not an infinite loop: every call is bounded at one read and at most two Decider choices, and the observed Run 2 used one. No generalization to any other case, fixture, endpoint, model or workload. Each elapsed-time comparison recorded here is one observation at n = 1, not a general latency improvement claim.
identifiers_note: Generated from the private records through an allowlist. No account, resource, runtime, endpoint, session, request, decision, call or receipt identifier, no hash or digest, no model revision, no version, no path, no timestamp and no raw model output is carried.

measured_latency.what_this_measures: One comparison per surface between the superseded post-D1 flow and the pre-selection flow on the same synthetic case. Client time is the caller's wall time for one runtime invocation. Selector time is the measured Decider inference time, summed over the inferences a call made.
measured_latency.basis: n = 1: the same synthetic case, each proof run once; the superseded post-D1 Run 2 is a separate earlier run of the superseded flow on the same endpoint
measured_latency.run_1_is_not_saved: Run 1 pays the learning cost once and is unchanged by the pre-selection block: one Decider inference, one read, unresolved, receipt stored. Run 1 is never presented as a saving, and no saving is claimed for it.
measured_latency.no_dollar_saving: No dollar or cost saving is measured and none is claimed: the Decider is served by a real-time endpoint billed by instance uptime, not per request. What the pair shows is one fewer inference, less occupied model time, and a lower observed Run 2 elapsed time on this one case, at n = 1.

earlier_evidence: Two earlier results stand and are superseded as the lead claim, not erased. The post-D1 proof ran the same case through the superseded flow: Decider 2B was offered the full option set, repeated the proven dead end, the controller refused that exact repeat before any read, and a second Decider call chose inspect_schema_keys, so Run 2 there spent two inferences instead of one. Before that, a two-read cloud pair showed one fewer read on a single pair once the bound allowed two reads, which is efficiency only and cannot show an escape.
